html:
The Konark Sun Temple is a 13th century Hindu temple to the sun god Surya on the coast of Odisha in eastern India, built around 1250 by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

The whole temple is carved as the god's chariot. It stands on 24 great stone wheels, each about three metres across, and is pulled by seven stone horses. The wheels work as sundials. The walls are covered with dancers, musicians, animals, battle scenes and erotic couples.

The tall tower over the shrine fell long ago. What stands today is the great hall in front of it, filled with sand and sealed by the British in 1903 to stop it falling too. European sailors called it the Black Pagoda and used it as a landmark.

It is a high point of the Kalinga style of Odisha, with the Jagannath temple at Puri nearby, and ranks with Khajuraho among India's great temples. It became a World Heritage Site in 1984.
sum: The Konark Sun Temple is a 13th century Hindu temple to the sun god Surya on the coast of Odisha in eastern India, built around 1250 by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
